question: A 65-year-old man presents with complaints of weakness and swollen gums for the past 3 weeks. He also says he cut his finger while cooking, and the bleeding took more than 10 minutes to stop. He has a family history of diabetes mellitus type 2 and prostate cancer. Current medications are multivitamin. His blood pressure is 122/67 mm Hg, the respiratory rate is 13/min, and the temperature is 36.7°C (98.0°F). On physical examination, the patient seems pale and lethargic. On cardiac exam, a pulmonary valve flow murmur is heard. There is significant hepatosplenomegaly present, and several oral mucosal petechiae in the oral cavity are noted. Gum hypertrophy is also present. A peripheral blood smear reveals myeloperoxidase-positive cells and Auer Rods. A bone marrow biopsy shows > 30% of blast cells. Which of the following chromosomal abnormalities is associated with this patient’s most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Myeloperoxidase-positive cells and Auer Rods on peripheral blood smear -> >30% blast cells on bone marrow biopsy -> likely diagnosis of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) -> 90% confidence. CHAIN: Gum hypertrophy and oral mucosal petechiae -> hepatosplenomegaly -> likely diagnosis of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) -> 85% confidence. CHAIN: Family history of diabetes mellitus type 2 -> increased risk for developing diabetes -> 70% confidence. CHAIN: Family history of prostate cancer -> increased risk for developing prostate cancer -> 70% confidence. CHAIN: Bleeding taking more than 10 minutes to stop after a cut -> possible coagulopathy or platelet dysfunction -> 60% confidence. CHAIN: Pulmonary valve flow murmur on cardiac exam -> possible cardiac involvement in leukemia -> 30%
enhanced_information: The patient's presentation with myeloperoxidase-positive cells, Auer Rods, >30% blast cells on bone marrow biopsy, gum hypertrophy, oral mucosal petechiae, and hepatosplenomegaly is highly suggestive of acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The most likely chromosomal abnormality associated with this diagnosis is t(8;14). Evidence paths linking gingival hypertrophy to hepatosplenomegaly and the association of hepatosplenomegaly with AML support this conclusion.
